newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebel attack on Sri Lanka police station kills 19.
newsitem.headline: Rebel attack on Sri Lanka police station kills 19.

text.p: Separatist Tamil Tiger rebels attacked a remote police station in Sri Lanka's northeast early on Monday, killing 19 people and wounding more than 21 others, security forces in the area said.
Among the dead were 11 constables, three civilian homeguards and five civilians. Homeguards are trained and armed civilians assigned to guard remote police stations.

At least 13 constables, three homeguards and five more civilians were wounded in the attack at Morawewa in the Trincomalee district, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo, officials said.
More than 200 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels are believed to have taken part. The two-hour attack took place shortly after midnight (1800 GMT) on Sunday.
"Many civilians were killed and wounded from the firing because they rushed out of their homes in panic and began running for cover," a police officer told Reuters.
At least three airmen were wounded when a group of rebels simultaneously attacked a small air force detachment at Pankulam, about 25 km (15 miles) east of Morawewa, the officials said.
Army reinforcements arrived on the scene shortly afterwards and the rebels withdrew into the nearby jungle, they said.
No details were available on the number of LTTE dead or wounded.
Spokesmen for the LTTE, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, were not immediately available for comment.
About 80 policemen had been assigned to the station, security officials said. A nearby police training facility, which housed about 150 trainees, was not attacked, they said.
The government says more than 50,000 have died in the war, now in its 14th year, although the rebels say the death toll is higher.
